line.comment: * SCRIPT NAME: Renegades.Monitor
* DESCRIPTION: Performs any slow running activities that need to be periodically performed.
* AUTHOR: Mr Mordan
* DATE: 21 February 2024
* Wait for starting options to be answered.
* Also wait for full generation of the galaxy.
* Add-Ons 1.2: Replaced difficulty getter with script call.
* Add-Ons 2.0: Replace those ugly X*60 with constants here. No magic numbers. Time is in seconds.
* The Renegade spawn timer is now dependent on difficulty. Increased default timer from 30 minutes to 50 minutes.
* Easy: 1 hour
* Normal: 50 minutes
* Hard: 40 minutes
* Insane: 30 minutes
* 1 Minute timer loop
* 5 Minute timer loop.
* Add-Ons 1.4: Commented out triplex removal.
* Add-Ons 2.0.2: Removed commented-out triplex removal.
* 30-60 Minute timer loop (Add-Ons 2.0: Time is now dependent on difficulty. 2.0.2: For debugging, time is every 5min.)
* set in z.cheat.cycrow.menu.xml, this is the player control to enable/disable autosave.
* save here
* Mordan4.
* Occasionally, player ships would end up with a bad relation set against neutral traders because you ordered them to attack one and from there on,
* those attacking ships would continue to attack neutral traders because they are set to attack-all-enemies. This avalanche is undesired.
* While I think this relations issue has been fixed in ship.signal.killed.xml, I put a safety check here to make sure none of our ships consider
* Neutral traders to be hostile and automatically attack as enemies.
* Every 30 minutes, possible spawn of a random Renegade. Scales based on player power and difficulty level of game.
* Late game, any new roamers will head straight for the player.
* If we were unable to acquire an unknown Enclave system at game startup, just return. Don't spawn anything.
* Player has set the global disable flag for renegades. No more roamers.
* plot has ended or station was never created.
* temporary. for debugging
* $playerPower = 5000
* Start raids once the player reaches a certain power level, but taper off later. Note, the average M2 destroyer is worth about 500 power points.
* MordanC - delayed entry of renegades plot.
* Add-Ons 1.2: Renegades are meant to be harassment ships. Having the power too high would make sense on easy and normal, but on hard and insane, the minimum power should be reduced.
* Renegade min and max counts are now scaled based on difficulty.
* Add-Ons 1.6.1: Max renegade count now scales based on galaxy size. 1 renegade per 10 sectors.
* Difficulty further scales the max number of renegades before they begin raids. Easy: 1 per 8 sectors; normal: 1 per 10 (default); hard: 1 per 12; insane: 1 per 15

* Min (default: 1500) and Max power threshold (default: 6000) is scaled as follows: Easy: 1.34x; normal: 1x (unchanged); hard: 0.67x; insane: 0.34x (roamers and raids start sooner). This is the same scaling as ZH.ScaleMilestones.xml
* Add-Ons 1.8.1: Changed max from 7k to 6k due to fixing double-counting capship fleet power bug.
* Default thresholds on normal: 1.5k min.
* Initially allow up to X Renegades to spawn as roamers.

* Add-Ons 1.6.1: Revised additional spawns. Once a certain number of roamers are present, start attacking the player's sectors. (1.9.4: increased maximum by 50% to give player more time to build before raids start.)
* Example: 75 sectors in galaxy and divider cap of 15 = maximum of 5 roamers. Additional spawns will harass the player.
* Is player power enough to start Renegade roamers? Even if the player's fleet power dips below the threshold, renegades will continue to spawn if the first has already spawned.
* Add-Ons 1.6.1: If the player lacks fleet power, isn't a nation yet, and the first renegade hasn't spawned yet, try again later.

* Note that we check the fleet power per spawn cycle, not per spawned ship. We also check supply. This is intended, as supply is slightly different (if player has Xenon or OCV ships) compared to fleet power.
* ** DEBUG **
* $t = 'Player info: ' + $powerAndSupply
* write to player logbook $t
* ** END DEBUG **
* Scale the number of concurrent spawns here: Easy: 1 per 60 sectors; normal: 1 per 50 sectors; hard: 1 per 40 sectors; insane: 1 per 30 sectors and minimum of 2 spawns
* Insane enforces a minimum of 2 concurrent spawns.
* Easy/Normal/Hard: enforce at least 1 spawn.
* Create up to Y renegade roamers at once.
* current list of Renegades in universe
* Are we exceeding the maximum number of renegades roamers? Or, is the player's fleet power exceeding the reduce raid threshold?
* Add-Ons 1.6.1: If yes, new spawns will start harassing the player. Set $seekPlayer to [TRUE] so that the ship will immediately head for the player to harass them.
* Add-Ons 1.9.4: Changed seek thresholds: must exceed rather than be at or exceeding.
* If player is over supply, ship difficulty increases by 1. Caps at 5 (scaled insane).
* This means they spawn tougher enemies, and even easy difficulty can run into an M7 if the player is overextended and fields too much fleet power!
* If we're seeking the player because player's fleet strength is high enough: increase difficulty by 1 tier. For example, normal will spawn hard enemies!
* Clamp. Should never happen anyway but just in case.
* find a sector to spawn in.
* Could not find a valid non-player sector to spawn in. Just return.
* Add-Ons 1.6.1: Don't return! We now spawn multiple ships at once, so move to the next attempt.
* ** DEBUG **
* $sowner = $RenegadeSpawnSector-> get owner race
* write to log file 1 append=[TRUE] printf: fmt='Spawning Renegade in: %s. Owned by: %s and Within 10 jumps of: %s', $RenegadeSpawnSector, $sowner, $StartSector, null, null
* ** END DEBUG **
* Spawn a new renegade. Alternate ship types with the faster one being rarer to spawn. Spawn an M6 on harder difficulties and an M3 on easy/normal difficulty levels.
* Add-Ons 1.2: Pulls from a larger ship list. (1.6.1 - can spawn 1 difficulty tier higher (including M7 if scaled difficulty is hard or insane) if player's fleet power is too high.)
* Tell the player when the first renegade appears.
* Add-Ons 1.14: now color-coded!

line.comment: * Start the ship task.
* Incrementing $shipCount is not needed at the moment but future-proofs the while loop for later changes.
* Increment counters.
* display subtitle text: text='Finding Renegade Player Sector' duration=3000 ms
* Add-Ons 2.0.2: This subroutine is called by CheckRenegadeRoamers. The galaxy is already defined there.
* write to logfile 1 append=[TRUE] printf: fmt='Random Player Sector: %s', $StartSector, null, null, null, null
* no player sectors found.
* display subtitle text: text='Could not find any player sectors for a Renegade test.' duration=8000 ms
* Build a list of player ship locations
* Now get a random sector within 10 jumps of the player sector above, that isn't owned by player etc.. and does not have a player ship it.
* Herobetty: if the player joined the OCV, then Xenon sectors are eligible. OCV sectors never exist, but they won't be exempt just in case.
* Add-Ons 2.0.2: ALL sectors are now eligible except player sectors and the renegade sector due to reworked roaming behavior.
* Does it have a Player ship in it?
* This is a safety check - by the time we commit to a spawning sector, we perform one last check as the player's ships may have moved by now.
* $t = 'Found valid sector: ' + $secinrange
* display subtitle text: text=$t duration=8000 ms
* write to logfile 1 append=[TRUE] printf: fmt='No valid sector found. Sectors within range of %s: \n%s', $StartSector, $sectorswithinrange, null, null, null
* Mordan3 Updates all Hauler's to show a display to the right of their name indicating the level of cargo they are carrying in percent. [] to [.........]
* Expanded 2.2: Freighter includes TS and TP.
* Expanded 2.2: Ported indicator improvement from FoF.
* From FoF - direct percentage readout, e.g. <60%>
* From FoF - ten-slot bar, e.g. <||||||....>. One | per 10% band, rounded up, so
* 51-60% shows six. Always exactly 10 characters wide, dot-padded.
* Mordan3 - Checks and updates total number of player owned beacons. We now restrict how many they can own, but there are too many places in the code
* where beacons can be killed, captured, and whatnot, to absolutely determine the player hasn't found a way around this restriction. Also, just the act of dropping
* a beacon (eject ware) from a ship doesn't appear to have any intercept point in the code that I can find, so we need to periodically update our count.
* are any beacons in systems the player doesn't own. If so, revert ownership to Neutral. If a player beacon is found in a Phanon sector, it is given to the Phanon.
* Add-Ons 1.4.6: Why remove beacons from unknown space? These are neutral - keep beacons there. However, remove them if placed in the renegade sector and the plot is not yet completed.
* Mordan8 - only convert player beacons to Phanon if we're not yet done with the Close Bonds mission. (See PhanonJumpBeaconConnected.xml)
* Add-Ons 1.6: Or convert only if Phanon has no beacons in that sector. Must not be allied with OCV (therefore, player is allied with Phanon).
* Hard difficulty, we won't allow player beacons in systems they don't own unless the player has X Notoriety or better with them.
* Mordan4. Rather than revert ownership and lose it entirely, we can just put it in the nearest outpost.
* Patch. Also, now allowing you to have beacon in Friendly territory, provided your notoriety with them is at least 3333 (level 6). (Add-Ons 1.3: On insane, 10000 notoriety (rank 7) is required.)
* see https://x3.solasistim.net/index.php/Reputation/ for list of notoriety rankings and values.
* Add-Ons 1.13: Cannot place if in permanent war. Permanent war can never be with Unknown.
* write to logfile 1 append=[TRUE] printf: fmt='Beacon found, sector owner = %s, notoriety = %s', $sectorowner, $not, null, null, null
* Add-Ons 1.3: Must have +7 reputation rank to keep beacon in NPC space.
* Mordan9 - Get nearest outpost within 50 jumps. (Add-Ons 1.13 - Use GetNearestSafeOutpost instead - it guarantees the nearest safe Outpost so that the beacon can be safely retrieved.)
* $outpost = [NULL]-> call script 'Mayhem.GetPlayerOutpost' : distance=50 sector=$sector
* Add the beacon back to the station. For consistency, replaced with library script call instead of "add product" and "add 1 units".
* Destroy the beacon.
* Add-Ons 1.13: If in permawar or in renegade sector, display special message.

line.comment: * There really is nothing to prevent the player from dropping beacons all over the place. There's no intercept point in the code.
* All we can do is passively poll how many they put down and delete extras.
* Add-Ons 2.0.2: Destroy as many excess beacons as possible.
* Any player ship smaller than M1/M2 class can not have a Triplex. Should a player transfer one to a ship, this will periodically go remove it.
* This subroutine is deprecated as of Add-Ons 1.4 since some Big Ships can have Triplex Scanner. It's too ubiquitous and easy to get anyway.
* get built in components and see if there's a triplex scanner. If so, remove it.
* = $ship-> add -1 units of {Triplex Scanner}
